PullRequest.Title: Use only verified terminal cwd for command approval
PullRequest.Body:

Replaces https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335978, rebased onto today's `main`.

- Send the shell integration nonce on cwd reports (`OSC 633 ; P ; Cwd=<value> ; <nonce>`) from the bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell scripts. The workbench already marks a cwd report without the matching nonce as untrusted, but no script sent the nonce, so every cwd report was untrusted and nothing checked the flag.
- Fix the fish nonce: it was set with `set -l` inside an `if` block, so it was gone after `end` and fish never sent it. It's now `set -g`.
- In `RunInTerminalTool`, treat the terminal cwd as unknown when its `CwdDetection` capability says it's untrusted, without falling back to the session or workspace folder. Relative file writes then ask for confirmation. When the capability is missing or the cwd is trusted, nothing changes.
- Agent Host's OSC 633 parser drops the trailing `;<nonce>` from `P` payloads, so the cwd value stays correct. Scripts escape `;` inside values, so splitting at the first `;` is safe.

Notes for review:

- After an untrusted report, the cwd is unknown for all of `prepareToolInvocation`: the `cd` prefix rewrite, the cwd shown in the confirmation and the sandbox input. The next prompt's trusted report restores it.
- Cwd reports through OSC 7, OSC 9;9 and iTerm2 `CurrentDir` have no nonce and stay untrusted. PowerShell runs the user's prompt after VS Code's report, so a prompt that also sends one of those leaves the cwd unknown, and relative writes always ask for confirmation there. This fails closed.
- Terminals whose script can't see `VSCODE_NONCE` also fail closed once they report a cwd.

How to test:

1. In bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell with shell integration, `cd` into a workspace subfolder and ask the agent to run `echo x > out.txt`. It shows the right cwd, and the write is still auto-approved.
2. Run `printf '\e]633;P;Cwd=/tmp\a'` (a cwd report without the nonce), then ask the agent for the same relative write. It asks for confirmation.

Tests:

- Added `Osc633Parser` › `Property (P) Cwd with nonce` and `RunInTerminalTool` › `should only use trusted terminal cwd when checking relative file writes`.
- `pnpm run test-node --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/osc633Parser.test.ts`: 28 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/electron-browser/runInTerminalTool.test.ts`: 224 passing.
- With the non-test changes reverted, each file has 1 failing test.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run oxlint` on the 4 changed TypeScript files, and `bash -n`, `zsh -n` and `fish -n` on the scripts: clean. PowerShell parsing wasn't checked locally.
- These ran with this change applied on `dbd1badaca92`. The 8 changed files are identical on `main`, and none of `runInTerminalTool.ts`, `osc633Parser.ts`, the shell integration scripts, `shellIntegrationAddon.ts` or `cwdDetectionCapability.ts` changed since.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `Cwd=<value> ; <nonce>` format and the trust decision come from the `Cwd` case in [`ShellIntegrationAddon`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e8b6d8b546735371b1d04237b0a7c40558ad82a6/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L583-L591), which already compares the nonce and passes `isTrusted` to [`CwdDetectionCapability.updateCwd`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e8b6d8b546735371b1d04237b0a7c40558ad82a6/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/capabilities/cwdDetectionCapability.ts#L34-L37).
- Putting the nonce last follows the existing PowerShell [`EnvJson ; <Environment> ; <Nonce>`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e8b6d8b546735371b1d04237b0a7c40558ad82a6/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.ps1#L135-L145) report.
- The Agent Host `P` split mirrors how its parser already separates the nonce for [`E` command lines](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e8b6d8b546735371b1d04237b0a7c40558ad82a6/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/osc633Parser.ts#L122-L127).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Static tracing establishes both report ordering in PowerShell and trust-only event emission, and the history consumer unconditionally serializes its complete cache. Storage equality checks occur only afterward. The prevalence of mixed-protocol prompts and the duration with large histories are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU for full-cache traversal, JSON serialization and downstream string comparison; temporary arrays, per-directory objects and JSON strings.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For P prompt displays and H retained distinct directories (bounded by terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.history, default 100), the mixed-protocol case adds 2P full-history rebuilds, O(PH) objects and O(PB) serialization work for B bytes of retained directory data. Storage coalescing does not reduce those two serializations.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated synchronous history serialization increases renderer-thread prompt-processing work and GC pressure, particularly with enlarged populated history limits.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Both VS Code's nonce-less report and the custom prompt's legacy report were untrusted. Once cwd/trust stabilized, redisplaying the prompt in the same directory emitted no cwd-change event and performed no directory-history serialization.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For a prompt emitting a legacy cwd report after VS Code's report, the new nonce makes trust alternate true/false on every prompt even when the directory is unchanged. Both transitions synchronously invoke the directory-history persistence consumer.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: shellIntegration.ps1:132 now appends the matching nonce to its Cwd report, before OriginalPrompt.Invoke() at line 152. If that original prompt emits OSC 7/9;9/CurrentDir for the same directory, shellIntegrationAddon.ts marks the first report trusted (589) and the latter untrusted (685/707/732). Unlike the base's two untrusted reports, these now cause two trust transitions per prompt; cwdDetectionCapability.ts:35 includes trust changes in didChange and fires onDidChangeCwd at 42.
Findings.Title: Avoid saving directory history on trust-only cwd updates
Findings.Impact: In PowerShell terminals with a custom prompt that also emits a legacy cwd sequence, repeatedly showing the prompt now rebuilds and serializes the complete directory history twice even without changing directories. Populated, enlarged shell-integration histories incur avoidable renderer CPU and allocation/GC pressure during prompt processing.
Findings.Evidence: TerminalHistoryContribution subscribes to onDidChangeCwd and calls getDirectoryHistory().add for every event (terminal.history.contribution.ts:59-60). TerminalPersistedHistory.add always calls _saveState (history.ts:111-115); _saveState allocates an entry object for every cached directory and JSON.stringify's the entire collection (171-174). Storage.set's identical-value check is downstream of serialization (base/parts/storage/common/storage.ts:278-281), so deduplicated storage writes do not eliminate this renderer-thread work.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep nonce verification and trust transitions, but deduplicate the directory-history listener by actual cwd value, or separate trust-change notification from cwd-history updates. Trust-only updates should not rebuild and persist directory history.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start an integrated bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell terminal and display ordinary prompts with only VS Code cwd reporting.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shell prompt hook emits its existing cwd sequence before interactive input; PTY output is then parsed by the workbench. Nonce handling adds no heavyweight initialization or awaited operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write OSC cwd reports through the existing PTY output stream to the terminal parser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same one report per prompt; only a delimiter and session nonce are appended. Fish also includes its existing nonce on command-line reports now that the variable survives its initialization block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cwd report and existing escaping/formatting operations without the trailing nonce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prompt-output processing; no additional round trip or separately issued operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cwd report per prompt per terminal; cwd escaping scales with path length. The nonce is a fixed session value, not a new key per prompt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hooks execute serially within each shell; terminal streams are independently processed. Existing bash/zsh command substitution and fish string-processing pipelines are unchanged; no subprocess is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The nonce is captured once. CwdDetectionCapability retains one trust flag and its existing cwd-keyed map; ordinary unchanged trusted cwd reports do not repeatedly notify consumers. No additional cache or lifetime expansion is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all four changed hooks and their prompt callers were inspected; added work is bounded string formatting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings collected. Minor extra protocol bytes are bounded by nonce length.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for ordinary prompts; report count, subprocess count and retained-key cardinality are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Redisplay a PowerShell prompt whose original/custom prompt also emits an unverified OSC 7, OSC 9;9 or CurrentDir cwd report.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Global:Prompt appends the now-trusted VS Code report, invokes the original prompt, and returns their ordered output. Workbench parsing synchronously fires cwd listeners on both trust transitions, including full directory-history serialization on the renderer thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Allocate the complete directory-history entry array and JSON.stringify it before calling storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full-history serializations per prompt after trust becomes stable between prompts, including when cwd is unchanged; O(PH) temporary entry objects and O(PB) encoded data work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both reports were untrusted; unchanged cwd/trust produced no event and zero directory-history serializations after initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous renderer work during terminal output/prompt parsing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update directory-history storage entries and timestamps; flush changed keys through the existing buffered storage mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four store attempts per prompt (entries plus timestamp for each callback). Identical entries are suppressed after serialization, equal timestamps can also be suppressed, and pending writes are coalesced per key. This is not four physical database writes per prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No directory-history store attempts for repeated same-directory prompts once both reports had stabilized as untrusted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache updates and comparisons happen synchronously; physical flush is deferred and is not awaited by prompt processing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P prompt displays and H retained distinct directory-history entries, bounded by the configured history limit (default 100), containing B bytes of directory data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two reports are processed in stream order; both history callbacks run synchronously. They are not joined or debounced before allocating and serializing. Database updates are subsequently equality-deduplicated and throttled by storage.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both reports refer to the same cwd, so no new retained cwd/history keys are required. Nevertheless, changing trust triggers onDidChangeCwd. Warm history still rebuilds its complete serialized state twice per prompt. Cold history additionally loads persisted state using the existing lazy loader.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: report ordering, nonce comparison, trust-sensitive didChange, the history event subscription, unconditional serialization, and downstream storage deduplication were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mixed-protocol prompt prevalence and serialization duration are unmeasured. Default-sized histories limit magnitude; enlarged populated histories increase CPU and allocation cost. Severity is low.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one materially amplified repeated-work regression. Preserve trust transitions while suppressing history persistence for trust-only cwd updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prepare a run-in-terminal invocation with a trusted terminal cwd, or without a cwd-detection capability.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Preparation awaits its existing Promise.all of OS, shell profile, cwd resolution and sandbox prerequisites, then sequential rewriting and a fixed parallel set of command analyzers before presenting approval information.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a local/remote cwd URI, activate/check its provider and call provider.stat through exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cwd stat per invocation with a nonempty supported cwd; no per-file-write cwd stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same cwd resolution/stat for trusted cwd and absent-capability cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited within the existing preparation Promise.all.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate the resolved POSIX shell path and, if missing, check fixed fallback executable paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for a custom profile or Windows shortcut; otherwise one shell existence check plus up to three sequential fallback checks on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same profile resolution, checks and fallback cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the shell-profile branch awaited before preparation proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check sandbox dependencies locally or via the remote sandbox-helper channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dependency-status lookup on a cold engine/explicit refresh; warm cached status avoids issuing it for subsequent prerequisite checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same cold lookup and warm dependency cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing sandbox-prerequisite branch; independent of the changed trust guard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Find bwrap/socat and execute a bubblewrap capability probe; read OS/AppArmor details when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bwrap probe when bwrap exists during a cold or forced dependency check, not per root or captured file write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited for cold sandbox prerequisites; cached thereafter.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the sandbox temp directory, resolve absolute permission paths through realpath and serialize/write one sandbox settings file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Temp directory initialization once; realpath per absolute configured/generated permission-path occurrence on a refresh (arrays deduplicated before/after expansion as implemented); one settings-file write per refresh. Warm unchanged command/cwd/network inputs reuse the file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same configuration keys, filesystem fan-out and warm reuse for this trusted/absent-capability scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold initialization and required refreshes are awaited by preparation/rewriting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One foreground terminal association per chat session invocation; one cwd resource, one command string and its captured writes. Shell fallback has three fixed candidates. Sandbox configuration path resolution scales with configured roots and command allowlist paths, not with file-write destinations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Four initial branches run concurrently; rewriters execute in order; analyzers run in Promise.all. Sandbox filesystem paths use existing Promise.all mapping, with output deduplication. This PR adds no limiter changes or new burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cwd itself is held in the capability, but getCwdResource performs an existence check each time a nonempty supported resource is resolved. OS/environment promises and sandbox runtime/dependency/config state are reused. Sandbox config refresh keys include command details, cwd and network mode; unchanged warm inputs reuse config.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the trust check leaves these branches unchanged, and the filesystem, dependency-probe and sandbox config implementations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote filesystem latency, configured path count and cold-probe duration vary; their costs are pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression: trusted and absent-capability preparation preserves existing work and concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Prepare a run-in-terminal invocation after an explicitly untrusted cwd report, including relative writes and sandbox rewriting.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new guard returns unknown cwd before getCwdResource and before session/workspace fallback. Existing profile and sandbox branches still complete, followed by rewriting/analyzers and intentional confirmation where required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The changed guard avoids the previous cwd existence/provider check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero cwd stats while explicitly untrusted, versus at most one previously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Attempted getCwdResource even with an untrusted capability, then used session/workspace fallback if necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removes an awaited branch operation; unknown cwd is passed directly to existing consumers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse or refresh the existing sandbox settings based on the command-cwd cache key, now potentially undefined.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A trusted-to-unknown input transition can require one existing settings refresh; stable unknown cwd does not introduce a per-destination or per-prompt refresh loop. Root realpath and settings write cardinality are otherwise the same as the trusted scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache compared resolved/fallback cwd; it already refreshed when cwd or command-specific settings changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required refresh remains awaited; no new boundary is added or moved earlier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One trust check per preparation, independent of the number of command destinations. Trust-state changes between invocations can alter the existing sandbox config cwd key; stable unknown cwd does not continually invalidate it.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing initial Promise.all and fixed analyzer concurrency are unchanged. No asynchronous work is started by the guard.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Untrusted cwd skips URI/provider/stat work completely. Stable unknown cwd participates in the existing sandbox configuration cache as undefined. A change between trusted and unknown inputs can cause a bounded existing configuration refresh; ordinary repeated unknown-cwd invocations with identical command details reuse it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the early return, downstream file-write handling and sandbox cwd cache comparisons were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of trust changes between separate invocations is unknown. Confirmation latency is an intentional approval behavior, not an independently established computational regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. This guard avoids I/O; its approval consequences are intentional behavior, and no concrete historical performance regression fix was established for internal blame reporting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host parses nonce-bearing OSC 633 property reports from PTY output and publishes terminal cwd state.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Raw PTY data passes through Osc633Parser.parseSegments; property parsing strips the raw suffix before unescaping, and AgentHostTerminalManager dispatches the existing TerminalCwdChanged action in stream order.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts: _handleOsc633Event Property case; agentHostStateManager.ts: dispatchServerAction; agentService.ts: onDidEmitEnvelope forwarding
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the existing TerminalCwdChanged action through the Agent Service action event and existing client transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per cwd report, with unchanged subscriber/transport fan-out. The corrected payload excludes the nonce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same action count and dispatch path; the complete raw property value was deserialized without stripping a suffix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: State dispatch occurs during PTY chunk processing; existing IPC delivery has no new round trip on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan for the first raw delimiter and deserialize the property prefix rather than the entire nonce-bearing payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra linear delimiter scan and at most one prefix substring per property sequence; suffix decoding is avoided. No collection-wide serialization is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Deserialized argsRaw directly, then split its key/value assignment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous bounded parser work; regular non-OSC output fast path is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One property event per incoming property sequence; string work scales with property length. Effective cwd action cardinality remains one per cwd report, not one per nonce or directory-history entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parsing and state dispatch are synchronous and ordered per PTY data chunk. Existing terminal-data flush boundaries preserve event order; no added Promise.all, subprocess or filesystem work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Partial-OSC buffering is unchanged and cleared when the sequence completes. managed.cwd retains the decoded path without the nonce; no new cache or retained nonce-indexed collection is introduced. Existing cwd actions are not newly coalesced or multiplied.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: parser fast path, partial-buffer handling, property consumer and action forwarding were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Property frequency and lengths are workload-dependent; no measured parser timings. Added bounded delimiter handling is not evidence of a material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression or proven performance-regression fix; this is a protocol parsing adjustment with unchanged boundary-call cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages against the supplied base. Traced shell prompt reporting, trust-sensitive cwd listeners/history storage, command approval and sandbox boundaries, and Agent Host parser/action delivery. Submitted one low-severity, high-confidence repeated-work finding for mixed trusted/untrusted prompt reports. No concrete historical performance regression fix qualified for blame provenance. Review was static and read-only; no performance timings were available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
